<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
So there are four separate tools at play here: `copilot-proxy` handles the local proxy setup, `copilot-model` modifies the project-level `.claude/settings.json` to include the proxy configuration, `claude-plans-here` adds the plans directory path to that same settings file, and `dot_claude/modify_settings.json` is a chezmoi script that manages the global settings file while keeping the proxy environment separate from it.

The core issue is that the project `.claude/settings.json` gets committed to version control (since it contains the plans directory), so putting the copilot proxy environment variables there isn't ideal. The user wants a clean way to toggle the proxy on and off per-project without modifying either the committed settings or the global chezmoi-managed file.

Looking at Claude Code's settings precedence — enterprise managed settings override CLI args, which override `.claude/settings.local.json`, which overrides the committed `.claude/settings.json`, which overrides the user's global `~/.claude/settings.json` — the natural fit would be to use `.claude/settings.local.json` for the proxy environment since it's project-local, gitignored, and has higher precedence than the committed settings file. The question is whether the `env` object merges at the individual key level or gets replaced entirely by a higher-precedence file.

Alternatively, a shell wrapper approach avoids touching any settings files entirely — something like a `claude-copilot` alias that injects the proxy environment variables when launching Claude. This gives per-invocation control: use plain `claude` for normal mode and `claude-copilot` for proxied mode. The tricky part is understanding whether settings.json `env` entries override inherited shell environment variables or vice versa. If the project's committed settings.json doesn't explicitly set `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, then shell env should work cleanly. This approach is smooth because it requires no file modifications, reverts instantly, and works across any project.

Another option is using Claude Code's `--settings` flag to load an additional settings file, which could be managed by chezmoi. I'd create a template file like `~/.claude/copilot-proxy-settings.json` containing the proxy environment block, then wrap it with a function that ensures the proxy is running and calls `claude --settings ~/.claude/copilot-proxy-settings.json`. The challenge is that if chezmoi manages this file, any runtime edits (like changing the model) would conflict with chezmoi's source of truth — I'd need to either use a modify script or accept that the file stays static and model pinning happens elsewhere. I've reviewed the copilot-api README and now have a clear picture of the design. The settings precedence flows from user-level defaults up through project and local overrides, with CLI flags and shell environment variables taking priority. The `claude-plans-here` tool specifically writes the `plansDirectory` configuration into the committed project settings file.

The core issue is that `modify_settings.json` manages the user's home directory settings through chezmoi, but adding copilot configuration there creates conflicts across all projects. The current `copilot-model` command pollutes the committed `.claude/settings.json` alongside the plans directory, which is the real pain point.

My solution uses two layers: a lightweight `claude-copilot` wrapper (maybe aliased as `ccp`) that starts the proxy on-demand and exports environment variables without touching any files—reverting is just running `claude` normally. For persistent per-project configuration, `copilot-here [on|off|status]` manages the gitignored `.claude/settings.local.json` file, which has higher precedence than the committed settings. The `copilot-model` command gets retargeted to edit `.claude/settings.local.json` when it exists, or fall back to a state file at `~/.local/state/copilot-proxy/model` for the wrapper's default model. This keeps everything clean: the wrapper reads either the `COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL` environment variable or the state file, and `copilot-model` gains awareness to edit whichever location makes sense.

I'm also thinking about the UX: presenting both the wrapper and the local-settings toggle covers different use cases—one-off experiments versus sustained per-project use. When `copilot-here on` runs in a git repo, it should append `.claude/settings.local.json` to `.git/info/exclude` for a nice touch. The wrapper should auto-start the proxy if needed, then pass through any arguments to `claude`. I'll update the documentation and follow the existing naming convention with `claude-copilot` for the wrapper.

The wrapper and toggle will set environment variables like `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, a dummy `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`, and the model selection. One subtlety: when using the sticky settings file, if the user has real Anthropic auth, the dummy token takes precedence; removing the file restores normal auth. Also, `copilot-here off` should only strip copilot-related keys from `settings.local.json`, leaving any other user content intact. For model storage, I'll use a state file with a fallback to `claude-opus-4.8` as the default, resolved in order: environment variable, state file, then hardcoded default.

For `copilot-model`, the behavior is straightforward: if `./.claude/settings.local.json` exists with copilot env vars, edit that; otherwise edit the global state file. I think the design is solid enough to present the full plan directly rather than asking clarifying questions first.</details></think>

## What changed

**`dot_config/shell/43_copilot_proxy.sh`** now has the two-layer design, tested end-to-end in both bash and zsh:

- **`claude-copilot [--no-specstory] [args...]`** — one-off session, zero file writes. Auto-starts the proxy if it's down, then launches Claude Code with the `ANTHROPIC_*` env injected strictly per-process (via `command env`, so nothing leaks into your shell). Per the plan's specstory note: it auto-wraps in `specstory run claude` when specstory is installed (same convention as `scode`/`svibe`), and extra args like `claude-copilot -c` reach the claude CLI through specstory's `-c "custom command"` passthrough.
- **`copilot-run <cmd...>`** — the generic building block underneath: `copilot-run specstory run claude`, `copilot-run claude --resume`, or any other Anthropic-compatible tool.
- **`copilot-here [on|off|status]`** — sticky per-project toggle via the gitignored `./.claude/settings.local.json`. `on` jq-merges the env block and adds the file to `.git/info/exclude` (Claude Code only auto-gitignores files *it* creates); `off` removes exactly those keys, preserves anything else you put in the file, and deletes it only when empty. Verified: the committed `.claude/settings.json` with `plansDirectory` stays byte-identical through an on/off cycle.
- **`copilot-model`** retargeted: edits `settings.local.json` when `copilot-here` is on, otherwise the global state file `~/.local/state/copilot-proxy/model` (read by the wrapper and by the next `copilot-here on`; `$COPILOT_CLAUDE_MODEL` overrides). `-c` now tells you which layer the value came from. It never touches the committed project settings anymore.

`dot_claude/modify_settings.json` and `claude-plans-here` are untouched, as planned. Docs updated in all four places: `copilot-claude-proxy.md` + zh-TW twin (new "Settings-layer design" section explaining the precedence rationale) and both `aliases.md` tables.
